name: Organic charge-transfer salts, control compounds
equilibrium_context: kappa-Cl: Mott insulator without superconductivity at ambient pressure. kappa-NCS: metallic, Tc about 10 K, further away from the Mott transition
summary: Internal control within the same material family. Shows that the effect is tied to the position in the phase diagram.

driven_states.emergent_property: Negative result. Under identical resonant vibrational excitation neither the Mott insulator kappa-Cl nor the metal kappa-NCS shows a photoinduced superconductivity-like response; the effect occurs exclusively in kappa-Br.
driven_states.source: Buzzi et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 197002 (2021), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.197002
driven_states.caveat: Valuable as an internal control: the effect is not generic for organic conductors but is closely tied to proximity to the Mott phase and to pre-existing superconducting fluctuations. This strengthens the electronic interpretation, but it does not replace an external reproduction - the positive and the negative result come from the same group and the same setup.
further_sources: Buzzi et al., Phys. Rev. X 10, 031028 (2020), doi:10.1103/PhysRevX.10.031028
